In accordance with Assembly Bill 361 (AB 361), City Council Resolution Nos. 2487, 2490, 2491, 2493, 2498 and
2499, due to the continuing state of emergency, including masking and social distancing directives as a result of
the threat of the COVID-19 virus, this meeting is being held remotely via teleconference. There will not be a
physical location for this meeting. Committee meetings are recorded for minutes preparation purposes. Members
of the public may participate in the meeting in the following ways:

- Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1-669-900-6833) from any phone, Meeting ID:
882 8363 1650 Passcode: 442300 (Please note you will not have the ability to speak using the call-in option from a
phone line.)

-  Public  correspondence  may  be  emailed  to  Carol  Corea, Administrative Assistant at
carolc@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails received before 5:00 p.m. the night of the meeting will be forwarded to
the Committee Members for their consideration and included as part of the record.

- Members of the public may comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos”
page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/agendas). Once the agenda is published, there will be an “eComment”
button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to the City’s SpeakUp page. After
you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda. These comments can be seen by the
public, will be considered by the Committee and become part of the record.

- Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store), by
entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 882 8363 1650 Passcode: 442300.

- Members of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video and may request to speak using the
following process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at
the lower portion of your screen. The Meeting Host will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each agenda item are available on the City's
website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city/agendas.

MINUTES
  TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE
  MARCH 16, 2022

1.  CHAIR ZUCKERMAN called the meeting to order at 6:05 p.m.

2.  ROLL CALL

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT:  Zuckerman, Brown Schachter,  Martin,
  Munday, Romanelli, Varner

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS ABSENT:  Boothe, Combs, Lum, Medawar

  STAFF PRESENT:  David Wahba, Director of Community Development & Public Works
  Joanne Itagaki, Traffic Engineering Deputy
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF TRAFFIC & SAFETY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES, NOVEMBER
  2, 2021.

COMMITTEE MEMBER MARTIN made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER
MUNDAY to,

  APPROVE THE TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES OF
  NOVEMBER 2, 2021.

There being no objection, CHAIR ZUCKERMAN so ordered.

4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON AGENDA

NONE

5.  DISCUSSION ITEMS

A.  VARIOUS AREAS OF CONCERN - THOMAS JUDGE EMAIL

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki provided a presentation summarizing the staff report. This item
is in response to a letter received by resident Thomas Judge, regarding four locations of concern
within the city.

  1. Palos Verdes Peninsula High School – Driveway 2

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that per a letter received from Mr. Judge, he suggested
that an asphalt curb be installed at this location so that drivers do not turn left (as posted). Collision
history was provided, and it did not show that there is a problem at this location.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that staff recommends that the existing striping pattern
on Silver Spur Road at Driveway 2 remain. It is further recommended that Sheriff provide selective
enforcement in the vicinity of Palos Verdes Peninsula High School particularly regarding the “No
Left Turn” sign posted at Driveway 2.

Director Wahba added that emergency vehicles may have difficulty making turns if an asphalt
curb is installed at this location.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BROWN SCHACHTER expressed her concern with the challenge in
having the Sheriff’s Department do selective enforcement in this area.

COMMITTEE MEMBER VARNER that he agrees with the recommendation made by staff.

CHAIR ZUCKERMAN stated that he agrees that selective enforcement is good; there being no
accidents may have guided staff’s recommendation. However, installation of a curb will likely
discourage drivers from turning left.

Traffic and Safety Committee Meeting  1
Minutes, March 16, 2022
 Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that she has no objection to installing a hard curb, but
there may be consequences to doing this. She added that it may impact the existing left turn
pocket for Silver Spur Road onto Hawthorne Boulevard as well as other traffic movements.

A brief discussion ensued on the various options.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BROWN SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE
MEMBER MARTIN,

  THAT NO CHANGES BE MADE TO THIS INTERSECTION AT THIS TIME, BASED ON
  SUFFICIENT SIGNAGE AND THE COLLISION HISTORY; AND, IT IS RECOMMENDED
  THAT THE SHERIFF PROVIDE SELECTIVE ENFORCEMENT IN THE VICINITY OF
  PALOS VERDES PENINSULA HIGH SCHOOL PARTICULARLY REGARDING THE “NO
  LEFT TURN” SIGN POSTED AT DRIVEWAY 2.

In response to a question by COMMITTEE MEMBER ROMANELLI, Traffic Engineering Deputy
Itagaki stated that Mr. Judge submitted a very detailed letter with his concerns about this
intersection.

AYES:  Zuckerman, Brown Schachter, Martin, Munday, Romanelli, Varner
NOES:
ABSENT:  Boothe, Combs, Lum, Medawar
ABSTAIN:

There being no objection, CHAIR ZUCKERMAN so ordered.

  2. Bank of America – 27411 Hawthorne Blvd.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that Mr. Judge had a similar concern with this
intersection. Collision history for the closest intersection to the location in question (at Hawthorne
Blvd. and Silver Spur Rd.) was provided; it showed that there were three accidents near this
driveway but were closer to the Hawthorne/Silver Spur intersection and not associated with this
location. In his letter, Mr. Judge suggested installation of an asphalt curb.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that staff recommends that the existing traffic controls
and striping on Hawthorne Boulevard at the Bank of America driveway remain. It is recommended
that City staff install an additional “Right Only” sign for exiting vehicles in the sidewalk area of
Hawthorne Boulevard at the Bank. Also, City staff will confirm the “Right Only” signs are posted
on the median. It is further recommended that Sheriff provide selective enforcement in the vicinity
of 27411 Hawthorne Boulevard.

In response to a question by COMMITTEE MEMBER BROWN SCHACHTER, Deputy
Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that the installation of an additional sign was staff’s
recommendation.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BROWN SCHACHTER asked if the emergency vehicles use the opening
to switch lanes. Director Wahba stated that it is used for this purpose.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ROMANELLI suggested that a right-turn arrow be painted at the
driveway exit in lieu of adding another right-turn sign. In addition, that staff verify that the “right-
turn” sign on the median is still there.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ROMANELLI made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER
BROWN SCHACHTER,

  THAT THE EXISTING TRAFFIC CONTROLS AND STRIPING ON HAWTHORNE
  BOULEVARD AT THE BANK OF AMERICA DRIVEWAY REMAIN AND TO CHANGE
  THE ARROW ON THE PAVEMENT EXITING THE DRIVEWAY TO A RIGHT-TURN
  ARROW. CITY STAFF WILL CONFIRM THE “RIGHT ONLY” SIGNS ARE POSTED ON
  THE MEDIAN.

AYES:  Martin, Romanelli, Varner, Brown Schachter
NOES:  Zuckerman, Munday

Traffic and Safety Committee Meeting  2
Minutes, March 16, 2022
 ABSENT:  Boothe, Combs, Lum, Medawar
ABSTAIN:

  3. U.S. Post Office – Deep Valley Drive and Silver Spur Road

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that Mr. Judge has concerns with people crossing and
vehicles coming in and out at this intersection. Mr. Judge requested to add or remove mailboxes
that are under USPS control; adding a mailbox at the CVS parking lot, which would require action
by the property owner and may require review by the City’s Planning Department if the number
of parking spaces are reduced.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that there is no recommendation required for this
request.

A brief discussion ensued on this item.

Director Wahba suggested a mid-block crosswalk to the Silver Spur Town & Country center may
be considered with the new development of residential units adjacent to the Post Office. Traffic
Engineering Deputy Itagaki added that this could be an opportunity to move or add a mailbox near
the new crosswalk.

COMMITTEE MEMBER MARTIN made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER
MUNDAY to,

  CONTINUE UNDER EXISTING CONDITIONS.

AYES:  Zuckerman, Brown Schachter, Martin, Munday, Romanelli, Varner
NOES:
ABSENT:  Boothe, Combs, Lum, Medawar
ABSTAIN:

  4. Rancho Vista Elementary – PVDN and Silver Saddle Lane / Moccasin Lane

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that Mr. Judge had a concern with the cross walk on
PVDN at Silver Saddle/Moccasin Lane and asked staff to look at the flashing beacon on Douglas
Street and Coral Circle in the City of El Segundo. The flashing beacon is an older technology; the
intersection in question has rectangular rapid flashing beacons and in roadway lights and they
are on both sides of the street. The collision history was provided and showed two accidents.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that traffic delays have increased due to COVID
restrictions, and this should return to a normal schedule in the next school year. In addition, City
staff has been trained and have done a good job with traffic control in this area along with the
school’s crossing guards.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that the existing traffic controls at PVD North and Silver
Saddle Lane/Moccasin Lane are appropriate. There is no need to revise any equipment at this
time.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BROWN SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE
MARTIN to,

  KEEP THE EXISTING TRAFFIC CONTROLS AS THEY ARE ON PVDN AND SILVER
  SADDLE LANE/MOCCASIN LANE; THERE IS NO NEED TO REVIEW ANY EQUIPMENT
  AT THIS TIME.

AYES:  Zuckerman, Brown Schachter, Martin, Munday, Romanelli, Varner
NOES:
ABSENT:  Boothe, Combs, Lum, Medawar
ABSTAIN:

B.  SILVER SPUR ROAD AT RANGE HORSE LANE - STRIPING CONCERN

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki provided a presentation summarizing the staff report. This item
was brought to staff by Mr. Robert Closson, who is concerned with the striping on Silver Spur

Traffic and Safety Committee Meeting  3
Minutes, March 16, 2022
 Road on the uphill approach to Range Horse Lane. People have had run-ins with the guardrail in
this area and he feels that it has to do with the striping in the area. The collision history was
provided and showed two collisions at Silver Spur Road and Range Horse Lane. Director Wahba
stated that the last time the guardrail was hit, it was a hit-and-run and no report was taken by the
Sheriff’s Department.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that Mr. Closson suggested that a portion of the “pie” in
the roadway at this intersection be cut/reduced. She stated that her concern with doing this is that
the pie provides protection for downhill traffic making a left turn onto Range Horse Lane.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that staff recommends that the Traffic and Safety
Committee discuss the concerns presented and receive public testimony.

The following is a summary of the recommendations presented in the staff report:

  1. It is recommended that skip yellow striping be added across the left turn opening on Silver
  Spur Road and Range Horse Lane.

  2. It is recommended that the edgeline along Silver Spur Road be extended around the
  northwest corner at Range Horse Lane with 12-inch white diagonal lines spaced 10- feet
  apart.

  3. It is recommended that 2 missing W1-8 chevron signs be installed on the northwest corner
  of Silver Spur Road and Range Horse Lane for uphill and downhill traffic.

Director Wahba expressed concern with the edgeline since it will limit on-street parking and
aesthetically, it does not look good. Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that she has no
objection in making the edgeline shorter in order to not impact on-street parking.

CHAIR ZUCKERMAN asked about the pedestrian pathway. Director Wahba stated that the
pedestrian walkways are very tight in that area.

In response to a question by CHAIR ZUCKERMAN, Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that
there are only about 8-10 homes in this neighborhood and not much of a demand for parking.

COMMITTEE MEMBER MUNDAY asked if Silver Spur Road was reduced to accommodate the
sidewalks. Director Wahba and Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki agreed that this did not affect
Silver Spur Road.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ROMANELLI stated that the crosswalk gives a false sense of direction
of where to go; he suggested changing the crosswalk to curve in the direction that the road is
going.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that she would need confer with Willdan staff to see if
this can be done.

A brief discussion ensued on this suggestion.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki revised staff’s recommendation, and stated that it is
recommended that skip yellow striping be added across the left turn opening on Silver Spur Road
and Range Horse Lane; that 2 missing W1-8 chevron signs be installed on the northwest corner
of Silver Spur Road and Range Horse Lane for uphill and downhill traffic; and that staff come back
to the committee regarding adding an edgeline along Silver Spur Road be extended around the
northwest corner at Range Horse Lane.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ROMANELLI made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER
BROWN SCHACHTER to,

  ADD SKIP YELLOW STRIPING ACROSS THE LEFT TURN OPENING ON SILVER
  SPUR ROAD AND RANGE HORSE LANE; THAT 2 MISSING W1-8 CHEVRON SIGNS
  BE INSTALLED ON THE NORTHWEST CORNER OF SILVER SPUR ROAD AND
  RANGE HORSE LANE FOR UPHILL AND DOWNHILL TRAFFIC; AND THAT STAFF
  COME BACK TO THE COMMITTEE REGARDING ADDING AN EDGELINE ALONG

Traffic and Safety Committee Meeting  4
Minutes, March 16, 2022
   SILVER SPUR ROAD BE EXTENDED AROUND THE NORTHWEST CORNER AT
  RANGE HORSE LANE.

AYES:  Zuckerman, Brown Schachter, Martin, Munday, Romanelli, Varner
NOES:
ABSENT:  Boothe, Combs, Lum, Medawar
ABSTAIN:

6.  DIRECTOR ITEMS

A.  UPDATE ON RESUMING IN-PERSON MEETINGS (VERBAL UPDATE)

Director Wahba stated that the COVID case numbers are coming down and the City will begin to
move to in-person meetings. The next Traffic and Safety Committee meeting will likely be in-
person in the City Hall Council Chamber.

7.  COMMITTEE ITEMS/FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

CHAIR ZUCKERMAN thanked everyone for their input and for the residents who submitted their
concerns.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki also thanked the committee for their input.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ROMANELLI asked about follow-up on his presentation at the November
2nd meeting on traffic congestion at Rancho Vista School. Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki
asked Committee Member Romanelli to send her an email with available dates and times to meet
with staff.

8.  ADJOURNMENT

CHAIR ZUCKERMAN adjourned the meeting at 7:45 p.m.

Respectfully submitted,  Approved by,
